svg.title: 4. Lifecycle and cost guardrails
svg.text: What it did for the example lake (monthly, us-east-1 list prices)
Cost by design: storage class per zone and age, and hard limits on what a query can spend
Intelligent-Tiering from day 0: Frequent, then Infrequent after 30 idle days, Archive Instant after 90
Noncurrent versions expire after 7 days (curated) or 30 (raw); incomplete multipart uploads abort after 7 days.
Clicks leave curated through Iceberg DELETE at 25 months, not lifecycle: lifecycle on a table's files corrupts it.
Minimum durations bite: Standard-IA 30 days, Glacier Flexible 90, Deep Archive 180. Transitions cost per object,
so lifecycle on millions of tiny files can cost more than it saves.
usage limit on RPU-hours per day
Flex execution for jobs that can wait,
after: stopped at the 200 GB cutoff, $1
Estimates from public list prices for the workload described in the article; check your own region in the AWS Pricing Calculator.
